analysis.title: The BEAT: Quarterly Global Market and Asset Allocation Guide, Q4 2026 - November
key_insights: Headline view is 'Rates Are Up. Growth Is Strong. Stay Constructive.' The group moves to overweight global equities versus fixed income, citing stronger nominal growth, AI productivity and corporate earnings.

Yields are rising mainly because nominal growth is strong. The group calls this central banks removing accommodation, not imposing restraint. Geopolitical, energy and inflation risks could turn 'good' yield increases into bad ones.
Duration is slightly underweight. The 10-year UST yield is back near 5%, the highest since late 2023, after the US-Iran MOU collapsed and oil rebounded. Nominal GDP growth is well above policy rates.

Credit is expensive. Spreads are near all-time tights, so the group is underweight investment grade and neutral high yield. It prefers MBS/ABS (stated as its highest conviction fixed income overweight) and bank loans, and is overweight TIPS.

US equities are overweight on earnings strength, AI adoption, fiscal stimulus from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act and deregulation. The US is judged more insulated from energy disruption than Europe. US small and mid caps are overweight versus large caps.

Europe is underweight because of Iran-war energy costs and low gas storage heading into winter. The preferred exposures are eurozone banks, utilities and grid equipment. Within eurozone bonds the group is overweight Spain and Portugal versus France and Germany.

Japan is neutral overall, but conviction in Japanese banks is upgraded. The group expects BoJ normalization toward a 2% policy rate, a rising nominal growth backdrop and capital-efficiency reforms to drive re-rating and higher ROE.

Emerging markets equities are neutral and divergent. Taiwan and Korea lead on AI-driven earnings revisions, China has weak domestic momentum, and India is underweight versus EM for lack of AI exposure and high energy costs, with its P/E premium near 100%.

EM hard-currency debt is cut to neutral because spreads are near all-time tights and fundamentals have weakened. EM local debt stays overweight through Brazil, where rates are above 13% against inflation near 4%.

Commodities are neutral. The Iran war lifted energy prices, and a resolution would likely cause a sharp reversal. Refined products, especially diesel, are the main stress point. Precious metals face headwinds from the Fed's hawkish shift and a stronger USD.

Macro backdrop is growth resilient or accelerating, sticky inflation with no wage spillover, a firming labor market, gradual Fed tightening and expansionary fiscal policy. The key risk is an oil supply shock that forces central banks to overtighten.
Core PCE has surged to 3.3% and drove the hawkish policy shift, but trimmed mean inflation still shows disinflationary pressure. Forwards price hikes from the Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoE by mid-2027.

2026 YTD global equity gains came from earnings, not multiples. MSCI ACWI 12-month forward EPS is up 30% YTD while forward P/E is down 14%, which the group links to debate over how long AI-driven earnings can last.

AI demand is accelerating with agentic AI adoption. OpenRouter token demand reached 113 trillion per week at end of August, and Nvidia's recent revenue guidance of 70% growth for fiscal 2028 was well above 45% consensus.

Cyclicals have underperformed defensives since July after the US-Iran MOU unraveled. The group remains overweight cyclicals on policy-driven structural tailwinds, and frames the open question as whether data weakens or the cyclical trade rebounds.

Alternatives: private equity neutral to positive, private credit neutral (prefer loss avoidance and special situations), infrastructure neutral to positive (AI power demand versus financing and permitting limits), real estate neutral to positive, natural resources neutral and the weakest complex.

Market monitor as of 10/31/26: 10-year UST 4.91%, 30-year 5.29%, US high yield 8.30% yield with a 344 bp spread, Brent up 19.67% in October, S&P 500 -0.87% for the month and +11.77% YTD, MSCI EM -8.05% for the month, silver -18.37% and gold -6.57% for the month.

Digital assets section shows Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana growth-of-$10K and correlations, and argues small Bitcoin allocations (1% and 3%) can change 60/40 portfolio outcomes. Digital Assets ETF category took in $4.5B in September on a one-month lag.

earnings_insights: Forward 12-month EPS for MSCI ACWI is up 30% YTD as of 8/11/26 (Bloomberg consensus basis), while forward P/E is down 14%.
Cumulative revisions to Bloomberg consensus for Growth/Tech are about +29% for CY2026 and about +19% for CY2027 YTD (estimates, as of 9/23/26). Revisions are broadening into cyclicals ex energy.
Nvidia revenue guidance (reported, per Bloomberg) is 70% growth for fiscal year 2028 versus 45% consensus expectation.
EM semiconductor forward P/E has fallen back roughly in line with the rest of EM while forward EPS continues to rise.
FactSet as of 10/31/26 shows expected EPS growth for S&P 500 and energy among the highest by sector, with 2025 EPS growth shown as the comparison.
Europe has the weakest EPS growth among major markets and is the only market more expensive since the Iran war began. The group expects EPS underperformance to continue.

risk_factors: Oil supply shock forces central banks to overtighten policy.
Inflation becoming uncontained, shifting central banks from removing accommodation to actively destroying demand.
Further Middle East escalation and energy price spikes, especially refined products such as diesel.
Spreads at or near all-time tights in IG, HY and EM hard-currency debt leave little cushion.
Durability of AI-driven earnings and late-stage AI valuations in venture capital.
Higher financing costs weighing on infrastructure, transport and real estate transaction activity.
Yen instability and a stronger USD as a source of global volatility.
Europe's low gas storage ahead of winter.
charts_described: Chart on page 17 plots the Retail Sales Control Group (real, deflated by core PCE) YoY on a 3-month moving average, with text saying real core retail sales keep growing at healthy levels despite higher energy prices.
Chart on page 39 plots trillions of tokens processed per week on OpenRouter, with the text citing 113 trillion per week at end of August.
Chart on page 26 plots Asia export growth contribution from AI/tech versus other exports, with text saying AI and tech account for roughly 70% of export growth.
Chart on page 23 shows central bank policy rates for the Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoE at current, Dec-26 and Jun-27, with text saying forwards price hikes from all four by mid-2027.
vol_and_positioning: Fund flows (Morningstar, September, one-month lag): large blend, large growth and large value open-end mutual funds saw the biggest outflows, while ultrashort bond, large blend and foreign large blend ETFs saw the biggest inflows.
Trading-Leveraged Equity ETFs had -$3,564MM of outflows in September.
The report includes a VIX history chart and S&P 500 stock correlation chart but gives no stated level in text.
geopolitical: Iran war and the collapse of the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding drove an oil rebound and an energy shock.
Tight refined-product markets, especially diesel, after a loss of refining capacity create a channel from disruption to inflation.
Europe enters winter with unusually low gas storage, leaving growth exposed to energy prices.
Further Middle East escalation named as a key risk to US equities.
Efforts to stabilize the yen and a broadly resilient USD described as containing a source of global volatility.
China's export surplus is widening in a 'China Shock 2.0' manufacturing export resurgence, adding competitive pressure on global producers.
Political uncertainty compounds France's fiscal problems.

tension_points.bull_case: Yields rise because nominal growth near 6% supports earnings, cash flows, employment and credit quality. Central banks are removing accommodation, not imposing restraint.
tension_points.bear_case: Geopolitical, energy and inflation risks can turn good yield increases into bad ones. An oil supply shock could force the Fed to overtighten.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Policy turns restrictive when fed funds exceeds nominal growth, and inflation becoming uncontained would push central banks to actively destroy demand.

tension_points.bull_case: Global manufacturing and services PMIs are accelerating and earnings revisions are broadening into cyclicals, so the cyclical trade should rebound.
tension_points.bear_case: Cyclicals have underperformed defensives since July after the US-Iran MOU unraveled and higher energy prices could disrupt the cycle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Economic data deteriorating instead of the cyclical trade rebounding, as the report frames the key question.

tension_points.bull_case: Trimmed mean inflation shows disinflationary pressure persisting and wages have not responded, so inflation is concentrated in AI and tariff-related categories.
tension_points.bear_case: Core PCE at 3.3% is driving the hawkish shift and markets price synchronized hikes by mid-2027.
